figures.caption: TABLE I. Explicit transition from the principal preceding interpretations to the claims supported in the present analysis. “Not supported” means that the earlier inference is not used in the current conclusions; it does not imply that the underlying stored score was fabricated.

FIG. 1. Direct domain and known-glitch controls under the coherent Q64 representation. Panels show held-out cross-run score shift, paired score change after native adaptation, out-of-fold run-probe AUC, and binary AUC for three labelled O3b glitch morphologies against held-out clean strain. Error bars are 95% bootstrap intervals.
FIG. 2. Coherent Q64/Q64 DSD disposition by detector and combined. Counts above each bar include every evaluated candidate.

FIG. 3. Sensitivity and baseline controls on representation-coherent, near-boundary samples. (a) Stability to native-background draw. (b) Rank correlation versus the production dictionary size. (c) Classical pixel baselines and a GW-specific convolutionalautoencoder negative control. (d) Candidate disposition under longer whitening contexts.

FIG. 4. Final replicated robustness study. Circles show mean pairwise Spearman correlation with 95% candidate-bootstrap intervals; triangles show the minimum pair. Near-boundary and unconditioned pools are reported separately for background draw, clustering seed, and dictionary size.

FIG. 5. Controlled native-index absorption for three injected morphologies and three clustering seeds. Lines show across-seed medians and bands show the seed range. Dashed lines mark the joint crossing rule. Experimental K = 282 dictionaries are distinct from the production K = 1216 index.

FIG. 6. Primary flag fraction for centred sine-Gaussian injections at fixed SNR 20. The dashed line separates Q ≤ 64 from Q > 64; the dominant blind region is at low Q, not uniformly above the representation boundary.
FIG. 7. Primary family-wise PEM endpoint with Wilson 95% intervals. All 141 selected events are calibrated; the intervals remain broad for the smaller coherent classes.

FIG. 8. Coherent-Q64 reassessment of the preceding L1 singleton. The left panel is the normalized Q-transform of the exact 32 s analysis window. The centre panel shows patch distances to the frozen native O4a dictionary; red boxes are the same Top-68 patches pooled into the stored score. The overlay is a visualization of this statistical score, not a morphology or causal label.
FIG. 9. Circular-shift coverage proxy for catalogue overlap. The observed two any-detector overlaps lie inside the null distribution; this is not a catalogue-recall measurement.

FIG. 10. Simulation-only compact-binary controls. Points show the primary flag, end-to-end physical coincidence, and maximum single-detector Robust fraction; binomial error bars are Wilson 95% intervals. Each point contains 25 successful injections into real O4a noise.
